primary_sources: Modern Tech Recruiting & Application Tracking Standards

rules.rule_name: Targeted Company Tiering and Segment Alignment
rules.explanation: Applying blindly to every available job posting without aligning with company scale, tech stack, and role maturity leads to wasted effort and mismatched opportunities.
rules.do: Segment target employers into strategic tiers (e.g., multinational corporations, high-growth startups, software houses) and tailor application materials to match their specific engineering culture.
rules.dont: Do not send identical, uncustomized resumes and generic cover letters across drastically different industrial sectors.

rules.rule_name: Systematic Application Tracking and Pipeline Management
rules.explanation: Treating job hunting as an unorganized series of ad-hoc clicks leads to missed follow-ups, lost interview schedules, and lack of performance visibility.
rules.do: Maintain a centralized application tracking board (e.g., Notion, Excel, Kanban board) recording dates, company names, contact points, application statuses, and interview rounds.
rules.dont: Do not rely on memory or scattered browser tabs to keep track of active internship and job applications.

rules.rule_name: Tailored Cover Letter and Portfolio Mapping
rules.explanation: Submitting applications without addressing specific role requirements or linking relevant projects fails to answer why you are uniquely qualified.
rules.do: Craft concise, impact-driven cover letters and portfolio highlights that directly link your past competition wins or projects to the target job description's core pain points.
rules.dont: Do not use robotic, overly generic template cover letters that omit company names and specific role references.

rules.explanation: Waiting passively after submitting an application through black-hole portals significantly reduces interview conversion rates.
rules.do: Identify engineering managers, team leads, or recruiters from target companies on professional networks and send professional, value-backed follow-up inquiries.
rules.dont: Do not spam company hiring managers aggressively or demand immediate status updates without professional courtesy.
